newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian privatisation revenue to fall below target.
newsitem.headline: Russian privatisation revenue to fall below target.

text.p: Revenues from privatisation will be up to one-third below targeted levels for 1996, Russian news agencies quoted State Property Committee head Alfred Kokh as saying on Monday.
Itar-Tass quoted Kokh as saying state coffers would receive only eight or nine trillion roubles from a targeted 12.4 trillion from sales of state property this year.
Interfax news agency said that the committee, in charge of selling formerly state-owned property, would ask the government to lower the target.

Kokh said last week that the government could receive eight to 12 trillion roubles alone from selling national power grid RAO Unified Energy System (UES) EESR.RTS Eurobonds and a 25 percent stake in telecommunications giant AO Svyazinvest.

Russia is facing a serious cash crunch, with tax revenues at only 74 percent of targeted levels in the first nine months of this year. October tax collection rates improved slightly to 84 percent of planned levels.
